issues.description: Check filename/CHANGELOG name mismatches metadata CheckID convention (positive vs. negative naming)
issues.detail: The CheckID is `compute_image_not_publicly_shared` (negation-form), but the CheckTitle is `Compute Engine disk image is not publicly shared` and the class docstring says the check ensures images are not publicly shared. Meanwhile the PR description calls it `compute_image_publicly_shared`. Pick one convention for the contract — either the CheckID asserts the desired state (PASS when name holds) or it names the violation. Mixing the two across CheckID/title/PR description/docs is a SPEC-MISSING smell: callers and report consumers can't predict whether `compute_image_not_publicly_shared` returning FAIL means 'the not-publicly-shared property failed' or 'the image is publicly shared'. State the naming rule once for the GCP check family and apply it.

issues.description: Silent failure on getIamPolicy violates the Image ADT's invariant: publicly_shared=False can mean 'not public' OR 'unknown'
issues.detail: `_get_images` catches every exception from `getIamPolicy` and still appends an Image with `publicly_shared=False`. The check then reports PASS for that image. Two materially different states — 'we verified no public binding' and 'we could not determine the policy' — collapse to the same boolean. This is a classic LSP/contract problem: the postcondition of `_get_images` is supposed to be 'for every image in self.images, publicly_shared accurately reflects its IAM policy', and the implementation silently weakens it to 'or we gave up'. For a security check this is the wrong default: a permission-denied or transient API error becomes a silent PASS finding. Either represent the unknown state explicitly (e.g., `publicly_shared: Optional[bool]` or a `policy_retrieved: bool` field) and surface it as MANUAL/ERROR in the check, or skip appending the image when the policy lookup fails. The current contract is unsafe by default.

issues.description: Image model's contract is under-specified: missing public_members, location, and self-link that the PR description and metadata imply
issues.detail: The PR description states the Image model has a `public_members` field, and the metadata declares `ResourceType: compute.googleapis.com/Image` with global location. The actual model only carries name/id/project_id/publicly_shared. The lost information is exactly what a remediator needs: which member(s) are public, and a stable resource URI. A downstream check that wants to say `image X is shared with allAuthenticatedUsers via role roles/compute.imageUser` cannot — the abstraction has hidden the only data that makes the finding actionable. Strengthen the ADT: capture `public_members: list[str]` (and optionally the offending roles) at extraction time, and let the check decide how to present them. This also gives you a clean substitution boundary if a future check wants to flag other risky principals (e.g., domain bindings).

issues.description: Service-level frame violation: _get_images iterates project_ids but is not threaded like sibling collectors
issues.detail: Every other late-stage collector in `__init__` uses `self.__threading_call__(...)`. `_get_images` is invoked as a single synchronous call that internally loops project_ids and then per-image issues a getIamPolicy round-trip. For accounts with many projects/images this is a substantial latency cliff that breaks the implicit contract callers have come to expect (parallel collection across projects). Either thread per project_id like the MIG/disk collectors, or document why images are intentionally serial. Right now the module boundary is consistent in shape but inconsistent in behavior.

issues.description: Test for image3 (Permission denied) asserts the silent-PASS behavior, locking in the unsafe contract
issues.detail: `compute_service_test.py` asserts `compute_client.images[2].publicly_shared is False` for the image whose getIamPolicy raises 'Permission denied'. This codifies the weakened postcondition flagged above. If you fix the unknown-vs-not-public conflation, this test must change. Worth calling out so the fix isn't accidentally reverted to satisfy the existing assertion.

issues.description: Check has no test for the explicit publicly_shared substitution path through the real service collector
issues.detail: The check tests mock `compute_client.images` with hand-built `Image` instances and assert on string output. There is no test that drives the check through the real `_get_images` extraction (i.e., the contract from API response -> Image -> check finding). That's the substitution the security check actually depends on. The bindings-with-allAuthenticatedUsers path is exercised at the model level in `compute_service_test.py` but never wired to a check finding end-to-end. A single integration-style test would lock down the contract across the module boundary.

review.summary: The Image ADT here is under-specified and its collector silently weakens a security-critical postcondition. The biggest issue is that `_get_images` swallows getIamPolicy failures and still emits `publicly_shared=False`, conflating 'verified not public' with 'could not determine' — and the service test pins that behavior in place. The Image model also drops `public_members` (which the PR description promised), removing the data a remediator needs. Naming is inconsistent across CheckID, CheckTitle, and the PR description, which is a SPEC-MISSING signal at the check-family level. The check logic itself is small and clean; the contract around it is what needs strengthening before merge.
